title: What are the parts of these two expressions?
description: Two expressions with taking away are changed into sums, their parts are listed, and their values are found. Keeko doubts the list and drops the sign from the number that is taken away.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away a number is adding its negative, and the parts joined by plus signs are the terms. Watch for children who list the numbers without their signs.

source: Write 13 − 2 + 6 and 2 − 10 + 4 × 6 as sums of terms, list the terms and find the values.
video_script.why: The child learns to split an expression into its terms before working it out.
video_script.substitution: Change each taking away into adding the negative number, then read off the terms.
video_script.anchor: Two expressions to split into terms
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko lists the numbers without their signs, so the number that is taken away is listed as positive two.
video_script.payoff_line: The values are seventeen and sixteen

final_answer.spoken: the first expression has terms thirteen, negative two and six, and value seventeen; the second has terms two, negative ten and four times six, and value sixteen

maths_rules: 4 × 6 has no plus sign, so it is one term
video_script.design: One idea: terms are the parts joined by plus signs, after taking away is changed to adding the negative. Assumes adding integers. Wrong idea: the sign is not part of the term. The two expressions stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two expressions: 13 − 2 + 6 and 2 − 10 + 4 × 6

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.pair: the two expressions appear one under the other
marks.ask: each expression is cut by thin lines into parts

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Look at thirteen minus two plus six, and two minus ten plus four times six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which parts does each expression have, and what does each work out to?

beats.on_screen: the two expressions stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 12 + 7 split at the plus sign into 12 and 7 with the label terms; 83 − 14 = 83 + (−14)

marks.def: 12 + 7 splits at the plus sign and the label terms lands on 12 and 7

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>The parts of an expression separated by plus signs are called terms.
<bookmark mark='change'/>To find them, we change every taking away into adding the negative number.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, thirteen minus two plus six, and two minus ten plus four times six.

beats.on_screen: To find: each as a sum of terms, the terms, and the value

marks.find: the words sum of terms, terms and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each as a sum of terms, list the terms, and find the value.

marks.one: the first expression is rewritten as a sum

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, change the first expression into a sum. Taking away two is the same as adding negative two.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The terms are thirteen, negative two and six.

marks.add: the terms are added two at a time

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the three terms. Thirteen plus negative two is eleven, and eleven plus six is seventeen.

marks.two: the second expression is rewritten as a sum
marks.list: the three terms are marked, with 4 × 6 as one term

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, change the second expression into a sum. Taking away ten becomes adding negative ten.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Four times six has no plus sign, so it is one term. The terms are two, negative ten and four times six.

marks.mult: 4 × 6 is worked out as one term
marks.add: the three terms are added two at a time

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step four, work out four times six first, because it is one term. Four times six is twenty four.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Two plus negative ten is negative eight, and negative eight plus twenty four is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The values are seventeen and sixteen.
The first expression has terms thirteen, negative two and six. The second has terms two, negative ten and four times six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows: terms 13, 2, 6; beside it 13 + (−2) + 6 with the term −2 marked; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the term −2 glows and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the terms of the first expression are thirteen, two and six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the two is taken away, so the term is negative two. The sign stays with the number.
